papers.title_en: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
papers.authors: Ruixiao Shi, Fu Feng, Yucheng Xie, Jing Wang, Xin Geng
papers.evidence: 免训练的视觉语言模型语义探针 GUI 元素定位框架
papers.tldr: GUI grounding 需在上下文中分辨细微视觉证据，而额外视图的价值取决于其暴露的证据与保留的上下文。SPARK 是免训练框架，利用 VLM 即使坐标预测错误也能描述可检查证据的能力，以探索与验证语义探针引导自适应裁剪和多视图观察，并用不确定性加权投票融合预测。在 ScreenSpot-Pro 上，它较单视图分别提升 13.9、25.2、16.1 个百分点（Qwen3-VL、Qwen2.5-VL、UI-TARS），并优于各骨干下对比的测试时方法。该工作将冻结 VLM 的“该检查什么”转化为更准确的 GUI 定位。
papers.abstract_en: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

papers.title_en: GUI-PRISM: Efficient Action Decoding for GUI Agents
papers.authors: Enqi Liu, Zhi Gao, Liu Liu, Lifeng Fan, Liyuan Pan
papers.evidence: 混合动作解码器直接预测GUI动作类型与结构化参数，实现指令到界面元素的定位
papers.tldr: GUI智能体通常把动作生成为文本，自回归解码带来明显推理延迟。GUI-PRISM提出混合动作解码器，用字段专用查询从共享多模态特征库直接预测动作类型与结构化参数，并通过条件查询建模动作组件依赖。在ScreenSpot-v2上达95.1%准确率，较最强空间解码方法高2.0个百分点，推理加速3.8倍。
papers.abstract_en: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents translate screenshots and user instructions into executable actions. Most existing approaches rely on vision-language models to generate actions as text, often leading to substantial inference latency due to autoregressive decoding. To address this inefficiency, we propose GUI-PRISM, a hybrid action decoder that directly predicts action types and structured arguments while retaining language generation for open-ended text. Unlike existing spatial decoding methods that primarily focus on target localization, GUI-PRISM extends direct prediction to action types and their associated arguments, enabling complete GUI action prediction. Specifically, GUI-PRISM employs field-specific queries to extract action-relevant semantic and spatial information from a shared multimodal feature bank. It further models dependencies among action components through conditional queries. Gated residual cross-attention refines these predictions using fine-grained multimodal information. GUI-PRISM achieves 95.1\% accuracy on ScreenSpot-v2, outperforming the strongest head-based spatial decoding method by 2.0 percentage points while delivering a 3.8$\times$ inference speedup over the baseline. On AndroidControl-v2 and MM-Mind2Web-v2, it improves complete-action accuracy by 4.8 and 0.7 percentage points while achieving 2.7$\times$ and 3.9$\times$ inference speedups over the baseline, respectively. Our code is available on our project page.

papers.title_en: RISE: Reasoning with Implicit State Embeddings for GUI Agents
papers.authors: Enqi Liu, Zhi Gao, Liu Liu, Lifeng Fan, Liyuan Pan
papers.evidence: GUI智能体将指令与截图转化为可执行动作
papers.tldr: GUI智能体需将指令与截图转为可执行动作，现有方法依赖显式推理，易过拟合特定推理模式而忽略可泛化的动作相关信息。RISE将动作相关推理融入隐状态表示，并用全CoT状态对齐、动作分布对齐和推理到动作边界对齐三项监督来学习隐表示。该方法在OSWorld-G达到70.6%准确率，较8B骨干提升4.3点，并在两个骨干和六个基准上验证GUI定位与动作预测效果。
papers.abstract_en: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents translate user instructions and screenshots into executable actions. To learn executable actions, existing approaches often rely on explicit reasoning during training, which encourage over-reliance on specific reasoning patterns rather than generalizable action-relevant information. In this paper, we propose an implicit framework, RISE, which integrates action-relevant reasoning into implicit state representations to guide GUI action prediction. To this end, action-relevant reasoning is captured through three complementary supervision objectives: full-CoT state alignment preserves information across the reasoning process, action-distribution alignment encodes action preferences, and reasoning-to-action boundary alignment captures the representation immediately before action generation. In this case, our RISE effectively learns informative implicit representations, thereby improving the accuracy of next-action token prediction. RISE achieves 70.6\% accuracy on OSWorld-G, establishing state-of-the-art performance among compared 8B models with a 4.3-point gain over its backbone. Results across two distinct backbones and six diverse benchmarks further demonstrate its effectiveness in GUI grounding and action prediction. Our code is available on our project page.

papers.title_en: GUI-WEdit and GUI-SkillEvo: Gradient-Free Adaptation of Small GUI Agents
papers.authors: Haixia Bi, Yingtian Chen, Sihan Yang, Zuzheng Kuang, Yuzhen Tong, Kai Fu, Zhengyong Wan
papers.evidence: 面向桌面工作流的小型GUI智能体无梯度适配，并在OSWorld上评测
papers.tldr: 小型GUI智能体可执行桌面工作流，但局部错误重复和流程决策脆弱影响可靠性。作者提出GUI-WEdit-4B与GUI-SkillEvo-2B两种无梯度适配：前者用轨迹反馈对末端MLP做受保护闭式更新，后者由助手迭代提出并精炼程序性技能且冻结权重。在OSWorld排除Google Drive的361任务子集上，两系统最终总分分别为48.02%和45.47%。该工作以极少参数改动和技能进化提升小模型GUI智能体可靠性。
papers.abstract_en: Small graphical user interface (GUI) agents can execute desktop workflows, but repeated local errors and fragile procedural decisions limit their reliability. We present GUI-WEdit-4B and GUI-SkillEvo-2B, two gradient-free adaptations of GUI-Owl-1.5 backbones. For the 4B model, we use trajectory feedback to construct guarded, closed-form updates to a late multilayer perceptron (MLP), retaining successful states as protection constraints. The final checkpoint changes 23,739,095 parameter values, or 0.535\% of the 4,437,815,808-parameter backbone, within one weight tensor. For the 2B model, an assistant iteratively proposes and refines procedural skills while the model weights remain fixed. On the 361-task OSWorld subset excluding Google Drive tasks, the frozen systems obtain final aggregate scores of 48.02\% and 45.47\%, respectively.

papers.title_en: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
papers.authors: Qingle Liu, Jieming Li, Pei-lin Li, Shenghan Zheng, Ruize Yang, Sunqi Fan, Deyao Hong, Huan-ang Gao, Meng-Hao Guo, Shuojin Yang
papers.evidence: 面向计算机使用智能体的在线基准，统一数字与物理世界的UI测试环境
papers.tldr: 现有ICL评测多为离线、文本或静态图像，机器人评测也仅限方法级消融，难以衡量智能体从数字到物理世界的上下文学习。作者提出在线基准ICLWorld与统一环境接口UIverse，构建30个环境、630段演示视频和160个含反直觉规则的任务，规则以文本或视频给出并分三级泛化测试。六个前沿模型中，电脑使用成功率最高82%，机器人使用仅约27%，无规则对照降至8%以下。结果揭示数字与物理世界、以及“识别规则”与“执行规则”之间的显著差距。
papers.abstract_en: In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time. The same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots, yet their ICL remains insufficiently assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface. We build 30 environments, record 630 demonstration videos (10+ hours), and design 160 tasks with customized, often counter-intuitive rules that cannot be satisfied without learning from the context. Each task comes with three rule versions, given as text or video, and we test generalization at three levels, from replaying the demonstration to new instances and unseen environments. Across six frontier models, the strongest agents, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, succeed on 82% and 76% of computer-use runs but only 27% and 26% of robot-use runs, and a no-rule control reduces success to at most 8%. GPT-6 Astra succeeds under all three rule versions on only 38% of computer-use tasks, half its rate under a single rule, and answers 98% of robot rule questions correctly yet completes only 20% of these tasks. Frontier agents learn rules comparably well from video and from text and transfer them across environments, whereas weaker agents rely on text and lose most of their video-based success once the demonstrated situation is resampled. These findings reveal substantial gaps between the digital and the physical world and between identifying a rule and acting on it.

papers.title_en: FigmaEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents in Professional UI Design
papers.authors: Xinyue Huang, Yongyong Gao, Zhengyuan Pan, Zheng Wei, Xinya Liu, Duanyi Yan, Zhiyu Hang, Zheng Ma, Lewei Lu
papers.evidence: 基于真实Figma文件的专业UI设计AI智能体基准
papers.tldr: AI代理已能用Figma自主设计UI，但开放式设计缺乏唯一真值，评估困难。FigmaEval构建84个任务、783个界面的基准，采用约束规格、开放方案范式，并设计22条六维专家评分规则与人类盲评竞技场。评测11个模型发现，规则评分与设计师偏好高度一致，不同模型在实践与质量—效率权衡上差异明显。该基准为系统评估专业UI设计能力提供框架。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in AI agents have enabled autonomous UI design using professional tools such as Figma, yet evaluating their design capabilities remains challenging due to the open-ended nature of design tasks and the absence of unique ground truths. We introduce FigmaEval, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design tasks, comprising 84 tasks and 783 screens derived from real-world Figma design files. FigmaEval adopts a constrained-specification, open-solution paradigm, standardizing task requirements and design resources while allowing agents to independently determine layouts, visual hierarchies, component composition, and visual presentation. To assess design quality beyond reference similarity, we develop 22 expert-grounded evaluation rubrics across six dimensions and introduce a human evaluation arena where professional designers compare agent-generated designs through blinded pairwise judgments. Evaluating eleven models under a unified Figma agent setup, we find substantial agreement between rubric-based assessments and human preferences, alongside distinct differences in design practices and quality--efficiency trade-offs. FigmaEval provides a framework for systematically assessing professional UI design capabilities and understanding the strengths and limitations of current AI agents.

papers.authors: Ross Murphy, Marcel Hedman, Gabriel Brostow
papers.evidence: 以鼠标键盘动作驱动桌面屏幕的生成建模
papers.tldr: 现有计算机界面被视为固定，用户或AI代理只能被动适应，难以支持个性化流程、免手操作或残障需求。作者提出交互式神经计算机：不训练代理操作电脑，而让生成模型充当电脑，根据历史屏幕及鼠标键盘动作预测下一屏。模型借鉴神经图灵机，结合惊喜门控槽记忆、VLM查询桥与残差渲染器，端到端从像素和动作学习。闭环测试中遮挡文件回忆率达64.2%，终端文字OCR从1.3%升至50.1%，且显式记忆可在测试时移植并因果改变渲染结果。
papers.abstract_en: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability. We explore an overlooked alternative. Rather than training an agent to operate an existing computer, we train a generative model to be the computer, predicting each next screen from past screens and the user's mouse and keyboard actions. Treating a desktop as an interactive world model raises problems that natural-video world models largely avoid. Without a camera pose to index memory, the model must remember content that has left the screen without any geometric cues. Arithmetic in a terminal has to be exactly right, not merely plausible. Small interface text must also stay legible at interactive frame rates. Our Interactive Neural Computer is structured like a Neural Turing Machine and starts to address these problems with three modules trained end to end from pixels and actions. A surprise-gated slot memory, supervised by latent next-frame prediction (MEMORY-JEPA), stores what is off screen. An exploratory query bridge brings in the reasoning of a pretrained VLM, and a residual renderer predicts only the latent changes between frames. In long closed-loop rollouts, our model recalls occluded files in 64.2% of trials (chance is 33.3%), compared with at most 56.0% for recurrent and sliding-window baselines. It also raises terminal-text OCR accuracy from 1.3% to 50.1%. Finally, because the memory is explicit, it can be transplanted at test time to causally change what the model renders.

papers.title_en: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
papers.authors: Vincent Koc, Aditya Washikar, Rishab Naveen Venkataraman, Onur Solmaz, Zhentong Fan, Xinyang Han, Toby Vincent John, Hao Li, Achyut Mukund, Biresh Chandra Biswas, Eshan Shukla, Louis Pan, Ivan Kudryavtsev, Patthigulla Sai Surendra, Krish Oberoi, Ayaan Zaidi, Hema Veeradhi, Taylor Agarwal, Erik Erlandson, Agustin Rivera, Jacob Tomlinson, Louka Ewington-Pitsos
papers.evidence: 面向真实日常计算机任务的智能体基准与评测协议
papers.tldr: AI智能体普及后，用户难判断模型与运行框架哪种配置更有效。ShellBench基于超1000万请求构建100个日常任务，置于杂乱文件和竞争数据源的真实工作区，并按正确性与安全性评分。评估12个模型、5种harness、3档推理共53100次rollout，发现模型选择影响大于harness，但前三模型仅差1.1个百分点。GPT-6.1 Sol以约GPT-6 Astra六分之一估计token成本通过61.4%，后者62.5%领先，harness影响很小。
papers.abstract_en: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% of attempts at about one-sixth of GPT-6 Astra's estimated token cost per attempt, while GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%. We also found that harness choice had little effect on either performance or safety with all harnesses scoring between 42.9 (Claude Code) and 45.2 (OpenClaw) for pass@1.
